name: stri_subset_fixed
title: Select Elements that Match a Given Pattern

origin.description: Keep the strings that contain a literal pattern.
origin.usage: stri_subset_fixed(str, pattern, omit_na = FALSE, negate = FALSE, ..., opts_fixed = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector to subset. The result is no longer than this vector.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Literal patterns. The pattern vector cannot be longer than str when str is not empty.

arguments.name: omit_na
arguments.text: If TRUE, drop missing strings and empty patterns instead of keeping them as NA.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, keep strings that do not match.

origin.details: pattern is recycled along str, but it cannot be longer than str. A missing string or an empty pattern is kept as NA unless omit_na is TRUE. An empty string is kept only when negate is TRUE. The string NA is ordinary text and is not a missing value. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
origin.value: A character vector, shorter than or as long as str.
origin.example:
found <- stri_subset_fixed(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "1")
cat(paste0('stri_subset_fixed(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "1") returns ', found, '.\n'))

translation.description: Keep the strings that contain a literal pattern.
translation.usage: stri_subset_fixed(str, pattern, omit_na=False, negate=False, opts_fixed=None, case_insensitive=None, overlap=None)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Literal pattern, missing value, or list of those. It cannot be longer than str when str is not empty.

arguments.name: omit_na
arguments.text: If true, drop missing strings and empty patterns instead of keeping them as NA.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, keep strings that do not match. An empty string is then kept.

arguments.name: opts_fixed
arguments.text: None, or a dict of search settings. Overlap is ignored.

arguments.name: case_insensitive
arguments.text: If given, match the simple uppercase of each code point.

arguments.name: overlap
arguments.text: Ignored, as in the installed function.

translation.details: pattern is recycled along str, but it cannot be longer than str. A missing string or an empty pattern is kept as NA unless omit_na is true. An empty string is kept only when negate is true. The string NA is ordinary text and is not a missing value. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
translation.value: A list of strings and NA, no longer than str.
translation.example:
from stringi.fixed import stri_subset_fixed
found = stri_subset_fixed(["stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""], "1")
print('stri_subset_fixed(["stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""], "1") returns ' + ", ".join(found) + ".")
